column1: # env.tsv (harbor#1431) — every environment variable harbor reads: its kind, default, meaning and owner.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. 408 HARBOR_* names were read in the tree on 2026-11-01 and 76 were documented anywhere; the rename register
# records a spelling change, never a meaning or a default. One row per variable puts the meaning where a reader looks for it, and
# bin/standard-inventory.sh holds it both ways: a name read in code with no row is red, a row nothing reads is red
# (standard.env-registered). docs/reference/env.md is generated from this file.
# WHAT IS NOT HERE. The files that read a name come from the tree (sh bin/standard-inventory.sh env <VAR>), so they cannot drift. A
# root variable, a path under the repos or the box tier, is a row of contracts/roots.tsv (scope.root-defaults reads it) and is
# registered there once; a name in both files is red.
# COLUMNS  var <TAB> repo <TAB> kind <TAB> default <TAB> meaning <TAB> stability <TAB> owner <TAB> controls
#   repo       harbor, or the repo whose own overlay judges the row (yard, fleet)
#   kind       switch | kill-switch | path | tuning | value | test-only | handoff
#              kill-switch turns a guard, gate or check off or to shadow; handoff is set by one harbor script for a child, never by a person
#   default    the value when unset, as the code spells it; - when unset means off or absent; computed when the code derives it
#   meaning    what the variable controls, in one line
#   owner      the family that answers for it (terms.tsv)
#   controls   kill-switch rows only: the controls.tsv ids it switches, comma-separated; - otherwise
